newsitem.title: FINLAND: New Finnish pulp futures show wary market - exchange.
newsitem.headline: New Finnish pulp futures show wary market - exchange.

text.p: The uncertain pulp market outlook manifested itself at the launch of pulp derivatives trade at the Finnish options exchange (Suomen Optioporssi - SOP) on Tuesday, the exchange's chief dealer Petteri Saarinen told Reuters.
SOP's world pioneer pulp futures exchange opened at 1000/0800 GMT but no deals had been closed by early afternoon.
The level of quotes showed that the outlook of pulp prices is uncertain, Saarinen said.
"The quotes are clearly below theoretical values; it seems the pulp market is nervous," he said.

At 1300/1100 GMT, SOP's March pulp futures were quoted at 543.00/556.00 and June futures stood at 545.00/558.00 SOPI. Theoretical futures values were about 556 points for March and 562 points for June, Saarinen said.

The pulp futures contracts are based on SOP's weekly northern bleached softwood pulp benchmark index which is derived from confidential industry reports. The index was fixed at 553.90 on Monday, down 0.35 percent.
The forest industry and analysts have said recently that pulp prices may fall in the near term, and not recover until late this year.
The 13-point gap between bid and ask price quotes was relatively wide, but Saarinen said he was not concerned about the early lack of trade.
"The spread is relatively wide ... but I would say it is slightly smaller than I had expected," Saarinen said. "Opening a new market is never easy," he said.
He said it was too early to say when the first trade could be expected.
